$doc: SHELL SOURCE ROOTS -- one home for the answer to 'what is the shell's source tree'.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: AuthSemanticsDriftTests scanned src/androidMain only, while
AndroidLogDriftTests scanned src/main/kotlin AND src/androidMain/kotlin AND both
template mirrors, quoting the Gradle line as its authority. Two pins, two different
answers to one question, and nothing compared them. That is a twin divergence in the
pins themselves -- see #364 F1.
THE CONTRACT: every consumer accounts for EVERY set, exactly once, as consumes /
delegated / excluded. ShellSourceRootsDriftTests asserts the three lists partition
the set list, so 'unmentioned' is not a state a tree can be in. Five separate reviews
defeated the auth pin by finding places it did not look; this is what makes 'it does
not look there' a RED.
IT BINDS, AND HERE IS WHAT MAKES IT BIND. Each consumer reads its roots from
ShellSourceRoots.SetsFor rather than from a private array of its own, and
EveryConsumer_ReadsItsRootsFromTheRoster reds if one stops. That fact replaced a
temporary one whose only job was to force this paragraph's predecessor -- 'these
entries record what a pin CLAIMS, not what it scans' -- to be deleted the moment it
stopped being true. LIMIT: naming the door is a TEXT test, not a proof the answer is
used, so a pin that calls it and then scans a hard-coded path anyway passes. Direction:
FAILS GREEN. It catches the revert, which is the shape #364 F1 was reported from.
A TEST NAMED ANYWHERE HERE MUST RESOLVE. `delegated.guard` is checked by
EveryDelegation_NamesAGuardThatExists, and every `reason` string -- delegated and
excluded alike -- is read for PascalCase_PascalCase identifiers by
EveryTestNamedInAReason_Exists. Citing a test in an exclusion is the same claim a
delegation makes; the only thing that used to separate them was which key it sat under.
DELEGATED IS NOT A SYNONYM FOR EXCLUDED. A delegation is a claim about ANOTHER test's
behaviour, and an unpinned claim of that kind is the bug class this repo has paid for
most often. Every delegation names a `guard` -- a test that asserts the delegate still
covers the tree. A delegation without one is an exclusion wearing a better word.
ONLY SHELL-TREE-SCANNING PINS BELONG HERE. A pin that names specific files on purpose
-- BnLogFormat, TextCollapseParity, DeepLinkSeed, DispatchSurface, GeneratedSymbolShadow
-- must NOT be repointed at this roster. Neither must ConsoleErrorDriftTests, which
walks every .cs under src/: that is the .NET tree. Sharing a walk is not sharing a
subject.
THE OTHER DIRECTION IS `scanRoots`, BELOW. The totality fact makes 'unmentioned BY A
CONSUMER' impossible; on its own it cannot make 'absent from `sets`' impossible, because
`sets` is where it reasons FROM. EveryShellSourceFile_IsInsideADeclaredRoot closes that:
it walks the scanRoots and requires every .kt and .swift file found there to sit inside
some declared root. src/BlazorNative.Jni/src/debug holds no .kt today -- only res/xml --
so leaving it out of `sets` is correct, and the day it gains Kotlin that fact reds.
NO NUMBER HERE IS FREE. `minFiles` must be at least 1 and at most `measured`, asserted, so
the floor cannot be lowered past the observation it was set from -- setting it to 0 and
re-pointing the container one level deeper was MEASURED green before that relation existed,
which is two JSON tokens defusing the whole mechanism.
AND NO `roots` LIST IS FREE EITHER. Every set carries `derivedFrom` -- the build file that
already knows that source tree, with the anchors locating the block and a pattern reading the
paths out of it -- except `androidTemplateMirror`, which carries `mirrorOf` and inherits
`androidShell`'s. Five Kotlin source sets come from build.gradle.kts, two Swift targets from
project.yml. EveryRootList_IsExternallyDerived reds if an eighth set arrives with a hand
written list.
WHY IT IS EVERY SET AND NOT THE ONE MULTI-ROOT SET IT STARTED AS: a root can MOVE. The file
claimed for three rounds that single-root sets were covered because removing their only root
takes them to zero. True of removal, false of rearrangement -- swapping `appleShell` and
`appleTestBundle` puts the shipped iOS shell in a set the auth pin EXCLUDES, and it was
MEASURED green, as were two more shapes. Every root list answering to a build file retires
the class; naming it would only have described it.
EACH scanRoot CARRIES ITS OWN `minFiles`, AND THAT IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. A single global
floor over these three containers is an aggregate over a partition, and it cannot see a
member leave: the template container is 18 files, which vanishes inside the headroom of
any total large enough to be useful. Deleting the whole entry was MEASURED green. So the
floor is per container and the total is derived by summing them. `measured` records what
was counted when the floor was set; `minFiles` is that number with headroom, so ordinary
deletion does not red and a container quietly narrowing does.
WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED, because the residual moved rather than vanished: a shell tree
outside every scanRoots entry, and anything under a declared `ignore`. Both fail GREEN.
That is disclosed here because a gap treated as covered ground is worse than an admitted
one.
TO ADD A SET: add it here, then add it to ALL THREE consumers -- the totality fact
reds until every one of them has said what it does about the new tree. That is the
mechanism, not a chore around it.

androidShell.purpose: the shipped Android shell -- both source directories of the Gradle `main` source set, one compilation, one AAR

derivedFrom.describes: the Gradle `main` source set's kotlin.srcDirs call

appleShell.purpose: the shipped iOS shell -- the BnHost target's whole source tree

appleTestBundle.purpose: the XCTest bundle. NOT shipped output. NSLogDriftTests consumes it deliberately as its positive-control anchor -- it MUST still hold live NSLog calls -- which is exactly why this roster has named sets rather than one flat list

derivedFrom.describes: the Gradle `androidTest` source set's java.srcDirs call

androidJvmTests.purpose: the JVM unit-test source set. Not shipped.

derivedFrom.describes: the Gradle `test` source set's java.srcDirs call

androidJvmHost.purpose: the desktop JVM inspector host -- InspectorHost.kt, InspectorPage.kt, InspectorServer.kt. A separate source set, not part of the Gradle `main` compilation, and it never runs on a device.

androidTemplateMirror.purpose: the generated app's shell. Ships to every consumer of `dotnet new blazornative`, and carries its own copy of AndroidShellBridge.kt

scanRoots.why: every Gradle source set of the Android shell project lives directly under here, declared or not. This is the container that makes a NEW sibling -- a src/foo/kotlin nobody added to `sets` -- visible.

the same shape in the generated app's tree. A source set that appears here and not in `sets` ships to every consumer of `dotnet new blazornative` unscanned. It is also the SMALLEST container, which is exactly why its floor is its own rather than a share of a total -- 18 files disappear inside 34 of headroom on any global count.

BnHost and BnHostTests are the two declared Swift trees; a third target added beside them would otherwise be invisible. `vendor` is ignored because it is where third-party checkouts land -- a vendored Swift package is nobody's shell. THE IGNORE IS INERT TODAY, measured: vendor holds a .gitkeep and nothing else, so that arm of the walk has no live exercise and this sentence is a forward-looking exclusion rather than a description of anything running.

androidTemplateMirror.reason: the template's AndroidShellBridge.kt is held BYTE-IDENTICAL to the repo's copy, so an auth change there without the same change here already reds. Scanning it as well would double every site and every ignored count in auth-semantics.json for a tree that cannot differ.

excluded.appleTestBundle: XCTest source. An authenticator token here configures a test, not a user's gate.
excluded.androidInstrumentedTests: instrumented source. The credential-path seam it drives is pinned in the shell by TheTestOnlyCredentialBranch_IsStillGuarded, which is where the guarantee belongs.
excluded.androidJvmTests: JVM unit-test source, no device auth surface reachable from it.
excluded.androidJvmHost: the desktop inspector host. It runs on a JVM, not a device, so there is no platform authenticator for it to name.

excluded.appleShell: Swift. Wrong language for an android.util.Log scan.
excluded.androidInstrumentedTests: test source; its own exemption is declared in that pin.
excluded.androidJvmHost: not the Android compilation. android.util.Log is not even on its classpath.

excluded.androidShell: Kotlin. Wrong language for an NSLog scan.
